raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Agent details Prepared with AI assistance. Preserve the weighted training objective while reporting detached LM, unweighted mean MTP, and combined metrics through the generic structured pipeline result API. Accumulate normalized contributions over microbatches and loss-owning DP/CP ranks, and use the LM term as the canonical validation loss. Depends on https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/200644 for plain `{"loss": tensor, "metrics": {...}}` results and the optional `loss_results` container. No public result class or separate loss callback is required. This draft intentionally depends on that unmerged API; it does not silently degrade when the provider is missing. Require one detached export per pipeline microbatch and consistent metric names before aggregation, so missing exports or terms cannot silently disappear. GraphTrainer remains out of scope. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/test_loss.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/test_validator.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_trainer.py -q -k 'not graph_training' ``` --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

 class TestLoss(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_mtp_reports_unweighted_auxiliary_loss_and_combined_loss(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(42)
+        predictions = tuple(torch.randn(4, 8, requires_grad=True) for _ in range(2))
+        labels = (torch.tensor([1, 2, 3, 4]), torch.tensor([2, 3, 4, IGNORE_INDEX]))
+        counts = torch.tensor([4, 3])
+        loss, metrics = MTPLoss.Config(global_vocab_size=8, mtp_scale=0.1).build()(
+            predictions, labels, global_loss_token_counts=counts
+        )
+        lm = F.cross_entropy(predictions[0], labels[0], reduction="sum") / 4
+        mtp = (
+            F.cross_entropy(
+                predictions[1], labels[1], reduction="sum", ignore_index=IGNORE_INDEX
+            )
+            / 3
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(loss, lm + 0.1 * mtp)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(metrics["lm_loss_mean"], lm)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(metrics["mtp_loss_mean"], mtp)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(metrics["combined_loss_mean"], loss)
+        self.assertTrue(loss.requires_grad)
+        self.assertTrue(all(not value.requires_grad for value in metrics.values()))
+

 ```
 
+The loss also returns detached `lm_loss_mean`, unweighted `mtp_loss_mean`, and
+`combined_loss_mean` statistics. The `_mean` suffix uses the existing chunked
+loss reducer's additive-contribution contract; the trainer reports the readable
+names `lm_loss`, `mtp_loss`, and `combined_loss`. Their normalization follows the loss call: each term
+is divided by its per-objective global target count when counts are supplied;
+without counts, the terms are sums. The weighted training arithmetic is
+unchanged. The trainer accumulates the normalized metrics across pipeline
+microbatches and gradient accumulation, then sums their DP/CP contributions
+on loss-owning ranks. Scalar pipeline loss APIs remain supported through
+PyTorch's optional `loss_results` interface. Each exported entry is a plain
+dictionary with detached `loss` and named `metrics` tensors; no result class
+or additional loss callback is required.
+
+Validation uses the LM term as its canonical `validation_metrics/loss` and
+normalizes its accumulated sum by the main target count. MTP remains part of
+the training objective; `mtp_scale=0.1` and MTP1 give
+`combined_loss = lm_loss + 0.1 * mtp_loss` for the normalized training metrics.
+
 Preprocessing also produces separate target-token and routed-token count
 vectors ordered as `(main, depth 1, ..., depth N)`. The trainer sums both
 vectors over the optimizer step. Routing counts reduce on every MoE stage;
